the non-invasive technique of whole-body NMR imaging can provide useful information in the diagnosis and assessment of liver disease.
NMR is more sensitive and specific in the detection of liver tumours and liver cirrhosis than ultrasound and radionucleotide liver scans.

NMR tomographic liver scanning is more sensitive than either diagnostic ultrasound or radionuclide scanning for the detection of space-occupyng lesions in the liver and more sensitive than either for the demonstration of cirrhotic liver.

the development of NMR tomographic methods in the diagnosis of liver disease, and with the application of NMR tomography for this purpose.
the development of a non-invasive method to detect liver disease and the demonstration of its value in clinical practice.
the application of NMR to the study of the human liver in health and disease.

the non-invasive diagnostic techniques of NMR imaging, ultrasound, and radionuclides liver scan all play an important role in the investigation of liver disease and that each technique should be used in conjunction with the other.
